candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: follow procedures for handling biohazardous and hazardous materials; apply infection-prevention principles
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — blood/OPIM specimen handling and labeling
candidate.educational_objective: Apply OSHA's specimen-container labeling rule and recognize the limited within-facility Universal Precautions exemption.

options.A: A recognizable specimen container may be exempt from individual labeling while it remains within a facility that uses Universal Precautions, but required labeling or color-coding applies when the specimen leaves the facility
options.B: Every individual specimen tube must always carry its own biohazard label even when it is placed inside a properly labeled secondary container
options.C: Specimen labeling is required only when the patient is known to have a bloodborne infection
options.D: Blood and OPIM specimens never require labeling or color-coding during transport or shipping

candidate.rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 states that blood or OPIM specimens must be placed in leak-preventing containers. A facility that uses Universal Precautions for all specimens may omit specimen labeling/color-coding while recognizable specimen containers remain within the facility. That exemption does not apply when specimens leave the facility. OSHA also permits individual containers to be exempt when placed inside an appropriately labeled or color-coded larger container. Therefore A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Recognizable specimen containers can be exempt from individual labeling within a facility using Universal Precautions, but the exemption does not extend to specimens leaving the facility; appropriately labeled larger containers can also satisfy the labeling requirement for enclosed individual containers.
candidate.source_locator: §1910.1030(d)(2)(xiii)(A): specimen containment and within-facility Universal Precautions labeling exemption; §1910.1030(g)(1)(i)(A)-(G): labels/color coding and exceptions
candidate.stem: Which statement about OSHA labeling of blood or other potentially infectious material (OPIM) specimens is accurate?
